title: Enforce byte bounds for inventory identity in model context
description: Sol review of PR #455 confirmed nearby properties/state payloads are removed, but inventory id/name strings remain unbounded in storage and tool writes. Twenty adversarially large identities can still exceed bounded-context or tool-output budgets, while truncating exact ids would make claim_item unusable. Establish write/storage limits and migration/repair behavior, then enforce a deterministic serialized byte budget without losing exact actionable identity.
design: Preserve exact IDs or fail closed with actionable repair evidence. Do not truncate an ID that a mutation tool must consume. Treat this as a general inventory boundary, not a nearby-list-only patch.
acceptance_criteria: New writes have reviewed id/name limits; legacy oversized rows are surfaced through controlled repair behavior; nearby context and pagination have a deterministic byte bound; exact claimable ids are never silently truncated; tests cover multibyte strings and over-budget pages.
